name: AgDevCo

other: Proven business model; full business plan and financial operating history for larger investments
Strong management team and long-term growth potential
Structured plan towards international ESG good practice
Excludes tobacco and potable ethanol
Low- and middle-income sub-Saharan African countries (upper-middle-income only with strong impact case)

how_to_apply: Email a business overview to investment@agdevco.com.
notes: Ticket range is from AgDevCo's 2022 press notice ('typically US$2m-10m'); a 2023 UK government guide cites $5-15m, so confirm. Portfolio includes Ghana and Côte d'Ivoire agribusinesses.

name: Root Capital

other: Agricultural business or grower organization creating positive social and environmental impact
Strong relationships with established buyers
Site visit and credit application after initial screening

how_to_apply: Submit the online inquiry form; eligible businesses then complete a credit application (decision typically 4-8 weeks).
notes: Ghana is the only West African country on the current eligibility list. Loan range ($50k-$2m) comes from Root Capital's West Africa programme press release, not the current apply page.

name: Shared Interest Society

other: Producers must be registered with a Fair Trade body (e.g. Fairtrade International/FLO, WFTO)
Positive balance sheet
At least one export buyer (producers)
Lends to producer groups/organisations, not individuals

how_to_apply: Complete the Producer Finance or Buyer Finance application form; regional staff usually visit before approval.
notes: Offers export credit (up to 60% of order value for commodities), 1-5 year term loans and stock facilities. Has a regional office in Ghana.

name: FMO – MASSIF (Dutch government fund)

other: Focus on mostly low and lower-middle income countries
Themes: the unbanked, agriculture and rural livelihoods, women and youth entrepreneurs, inclusive business innovation

how_to_apply: SMEs access MASSIF funding through the local financial intermediaries and funds it backs; intermediaries contact FMO directly.
notes: Instruments include seed capital, local-currency debt, mezzanine, direct equity, fund investments and capacity-development grants for investees. FMO also finances larger agribusinesses directly (long-term loans, equity, mezzanine, working capital); no ticket size is published.

name: International Finance Corporation (IFC)

other: Located in a developing member country of IFC; private sector
Technically sound with good prospects of profitability
Must benefit the local economy
Must meet IFC environmental and social standards
Does not lend directly to micro, small and medium enterprises

how_to_apply: No standard form; send an investment proposal to the relevant IFC industry or regional office (see IFC contact directory).
notes: SMEs reach IFC money mainly through banks and financial intermediaries that IFC funds. Direct financing suits larger companies only.

name: Development Bank Ghana (DBG)

other: Funds reach MSMEs and small corporates only via participating financial institutions (PFIs)

how_to_apply: Apply for a loan at a DBG participating financial institution (partner bank), which on-lends DBG funds.
notes: Wholesale bank providing medium-to-long-term funding to PFIs. The DBG Guarantee subsidiary de-risks MSME loans via PFIs. Focus sectors also include tourism and housing. The official site (dbg.com.gh) could not be fetched.

name: Ghana Export-Import Bank (GEXIM)

other: Ghanaian exporters and businesses in the export value chain
Show viable export activities or export contracts/orders
Business plan, financial statements, proof of registration

how_to_apply: Apply through GEXIM offices or its partner financial institutions; contact via the GEXIM website.
notes: Products include SME banking, export trade working capital and guarantees for SMEs lacking collateral. The 'up to $10m per transaction' figure is from a third-party guide, not the GEXIM site.

name: Norfund

other: Sustainable, profitable private company in an ODA-eligible country within Norfund's sectors and geographies
Minority investor: equity USD 5-50m with max 35% ownership; loans from USD 5m (3-10 year tenor)
Detailed business plan/proposal required

how_to_apply: Use the Norfund contact form, choose 'Possible investment' and attach a business plan in English or Norwegian.
notes: The Accra office covers West Africa, with focus countries Ghana, Nigeria, Côte d'Ivoire and Senegal. 'Scalable Enterprises' covers food, agribusiness and manufacturing.

name: British International Investment (BII)

other: Successful track record or extensive relevant operational experience
Solid business plan and experienced management team
Does not provide start-up capital, grants, export finance or sovereign lending

how_to_apply: Approach BII directly for large deals; smaller businesses reach BII capital via the funds and banks it backs (e.g. AgDevCo).
notes: Ticket sizes ($10m-$250m for direct equity and debt) are from a UK government guide, not the BII site. Debt and risk-sharing for SMEs flows through financial institutions.

name: Injaro Investments – agricultural SME fund

other: Mainly family-owned West African SMEs across the agricultural value chain
Targets firms rarely eligible for traditional bank financing

how_to_apply: Contact Injaro Investments directly with a business plan.
notes: Injaro is a West Africa-focused manager set up in 2009 and is also investment advisor to the ABC Fund. This is an older fund vintage, so confirm it is still investing.

name: Investisseurs & Partenaires (I&P)

other: Sustainable, profitable SMEs with high local added value
Minority investor

how_to_apply: Submit a business plan via the 'Submit a Business Plan' page on ietp.com.
notes: The overall range is EUR 10k-5m (converted at ~1.1 USD/EUR): EUR 50k-500k via partner funds (e.g. Teranga Capital in Senegal, Comoé Capital in Côte d'Ivoire) and EUR 500k-5m direct via the IPAE funds. Teams are in Ghana, Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire and elsewhere.

name: Agri-Business Capital Fund (ABC Fund)

other: Rural SMEs, farmers' organisations and smallholder groups
Commercially viable ventures creating jobs, especially for youth and women
Climate-smart projects prioritised

how_to_apply: Contact the fund via its website (managed by Bamboo Capital Partners, with Injaro Investments as advisor).
notes: IFAD-backed. Direct loans run EUR 200k-800k (~USD 220k-880k at ~1.1 USD/EUR); smaller EUR 20k-200k loans go via financial institutions. Ranges are from the fund's launch announcement.

name: Acumen West Africa

other: Validated business model with first customers
Impact on low-income people (breadth, depth, poverty focus)

how_to_apply: Apply via Acumen's West Africa page.
notes: Figures (first investment $250k-$750k) are from a secondary profile of unknown date. Agriculture and renewable energy were earlier focus areas. Confirm the programme is still active.

name: Aruwa Capital Management

other: Small, rapidly growing businesses overlooked by larger PE firms
Gender-lens investor

how_to_apply: Contact Aruwa Capital directly.
notes: AVCA profile states an 'average ticket size range below US$5mn'. Growth equity in Nigeria and Ghana; FMCG manufacturing and agri-processing are listed sectors.

name: Verod Capital Growth Fund III

other: High-growth middle-market companies in Anglophone West Africa

how_to_apply: Contact Verod Capital Partners directly.
notes: Details come from the 2018 AfDB approval of a $15m commitment. The fund may now be fully invested, so check for a successor fund.

name: Verod-Kepple Africa Ventures

other: Series A and B tech startups

how_to_apply: Contact the fund directly.
notes: The $1m-$3m figure is the average ticket reported by TechCabal in 2024. The predecessor Kepple Africa Ventures wrote $50k-$150k pre-seed/seed cheques. The sector tag 'fintech' is inferred from portfolio examples (e.g. Julaya).

name: TLcom Capital (TIDE Africa Fund II)

other: Primarily seed and Series A tech-enabled companies

how_to_apply: Contact TLcom directly.
notes: Initial investments of $1m-$3m from the $154m fund; also runs a small pre-seed cheque strategy. Offices in Lagos and Nairobi.

name: Partech Africa II

other: Technology-driven companies, Seed to Series B+

how_to_apply: Contact Partech's Africa team directly.
notes: Initial tickets of USD 1m-15m (EIB fund page). EUR 245m+ fund covering sub-Saharan Africa. Logistics is also a target sector.

name: Bank of Industry (BOI) Nigeria

other: Registered company or enterprise (no individuals)
Manufacturing/processing activity (agro-processing, solid minerals, IT, oil & gas, creative industry)
Collateral required; funds paid to equipment vendors
Startups considered case by case
Direct loans start from NGN 5 million

how_to_apply: Register and apply on the BOI online portal, uploading company registration and supporting documents.
notes: Finances equipment directly. Working capital goes via partner SME-friendly banks, and smaller loans via state matching funds or microfinance banks. The NGN 5m minimum is not converted because of FX volatility.

name: Development Bank of Nigeria (DBN)

other: MSME in a productive enterprise (start-up or existing)
Must be a customer of a DBN participating financial institution

how_to_apply: Ask a DBN participating bank or microfinance bank for a DBN-funded loan; the PFI assesses you and applies to DBN.
notes: Wholesale lender with 84 PFIs (Dec 2025). Tenor up to 10 years with up to 18 months moratorium. Also offers partial credit guarantees to PFIs.

name: African Development Bank – Affirmative Finance Action for Women in Africa (AFAWA)

other: Women-led SMEs

how_to_apply: Women-led SMEs borrow from AFAWA partner banks and financial institutions, which receive AfDB risk-sharing guarantees.
notes: The Guarantee for Growth programme covers up to 75% of lending risk for partner institutions in some cases. No partner banks in Ghana, Nigeria, Côte d'Ivoire or Senegal were named in the source.

name: Afreximbank – Export SME Development Programme (ESDP)

other: SMEs in export-oriented sectors

how_to_apply: SMEs access ESDP funds through Afreximbank's local partner banks (e.g. Ecobank in Zimbabwe).
notes: Provides working capital and capex lines to banks for export SMEs, plus export-readiness support. No West African partner banks were confirmed. The official site could not be fetched.
